name: Waters for Georgia
summary: Two-step grants (concept, then invited full proposal) for water quality, riparian and aquatic habitat restoration and barrier removal in selected regions of Georgia, USA. Open to nonprofits and governmental agencies.

geography.label: Georgia, USA (2027-2028 cycle: Coastal, Central and ACF/ACT regions)

pool.label: the 2027-2028 grant cycle
pool.note: Split between the regions selected for this cycle

eligibility.rule: Government agency, or 501(c)(3) (509(a)(3)(B)(iii) only if functionally integrated)
Not an individual, private school, religious organization, political campaign or cause
Have policies and actions that do not discriminate
Not be designed to mitigate legal or regulatory compliance obligations or ongoing legal action
Have a clear link to watershed and aquatic ecosystem health
Be within the Coastal, Central, or ACF/ACT regions

calls.label: 2027-2028 grant cycle
calls.note: Concept stage was scheduled for August to October 2026; the page states no concept deadline

status.quote: Prospective applicants will submit a project concept August - October, 2026

pool.quote: Total funding for this cycle is expected to be $1,500,000.

administered_by.quote: The program is administered on behalf of the Georgia Power Foundation by the Bonneville Environmental Foundation (BEF)

applicant_types.quote: The Georgia Power Foundation considers proposals from: Governmental agencies Organizations with active 501(c)(3) tax status

geography.quote: For the current (2027-2028) grant cycle, projects must be within the following regions: Coastal Central ACF (Apalachicola-Chattahoochee-Flint) / ACT (Alabama-Coosa-Tallapoosa)

access.quote: Submittal of a project concept Based on the results of the project concept review, selected project proponents will be invited to submit a full proposal.

window.quote: Grant cycles occur every other year (odd years), and focuses on two-three regions within the state.

effort.quote: selected project proponents will be invited to submit a full proposal

eligibility.quote: Governmental agencies Organizations with active 501(c)(3) tax status under Section 509 of the Internal Revenue Code (excluding organizations under Code Section 509(a)(3)(B)(iii) that are not "functionally integrated" with their supported organization)
Individuals, private elementary or secondary schools, religious organizations, or political campaigns or causes
Organizations whose policies or actions discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, religion, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, or disability
Projects designed to mitigate legal or regulatory compliance obligations, or tied to ongoing legal or regulatory action
All projects must have a clear link to watershed and aquatic ecosystem health.
For the current (2027-2028) grant cycle, projects must be within the following regions: Coastal Central ACF (Apalachicola-Chattahoochee-Flint) / ACT (Alabama-Coosa-Tallapoosa)

after_award.quote: Project implementation and reporting July 2027 - December 2028
